# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## I. By Primary Task Type

### A. Loop/Path Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws a single continuous loop or path through the grid.

#### A1. Pure Loop Construction
- **Masyu** – Loop through cells with black/white circle constraints on turning/straight behavior
- **Slitherlink** – Loop on grid edges/dots with numeric constraints on surrounding line segments
- **Mid-loop** – Loop through cells where black circles must be midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** – Directed loop with wind constraints affecting movement
- **Moon-or-Sun** – Loop through rooms alternating between moon and sun symbols
- **Suraromu** – Loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing through all gates in order
- **Dotchi-Loop** – Loop through cells with white circles (straight or turn per region) avoiding black circles

#### A2. Loop with Shading
- **Yajilin** – Loop plus placement of black cells, with arrow/number clues indicating black cell counts

### B. Path/Connection Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws paths connecting specific points (not necessarily forming a loop).

- **Numberlink** – Connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing, non-branching paths
- **Hashiwokakero** – Connect island nodes with bridges (1 or 2) matching island numbers, forming a connected network

### C. Cell Shading/Painting
Puzzles where the solver determines which cells to shade black (or leave white).

#### C1. Shading with Numeric Clues on Black Cells
- **Nurikabe** – Numbers indicate white island sizes; black cells form one connected wall with no 2×2
- **Kurotto** – Circled numbers indicate sum of adjacent black cell groups; circle cells stay white
- **Kurodoko** – Numbers indicate count of visible white cells in four directions; black cells don't touch
- **Heyawake** – Numbers in rooms indicate count of shaded cells; white cells connected, no 3-room white runs
- **Norinori** – Each bold-lined region contains exactly two shaded cells forming dominoes
- **Nurimisaki** – Circle cells are white "promontories" with numbered line-of-sight; no 2×2 of either color
- **Nuritwin** – Each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shading connected, no 2×2
- **Usowan** – Numbers show adjacent shaded cell count, but one number per room is wrong; shaded cells don't touch
- **Sto-stone** – Numbers in rooms indicate black cell count; black cells "drop" to fill bottom half of grid
- **Tilepaint** – Entire tiles shaded or unshaded; diagonal-cell numbers constrain row/column black cell counts

#### C2. Shading with Shape Constraints
- **Choco Banana** – Black groups must form rectangles/squares; white groups must not form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate area size
- **LITS** – Each region contributes one tetromino; same-shape tetrominoes don't touch; all shading connected, no 2×2
- **Shakashaka** – Place triangles in cells so remaining white areas form rectangles/squares; numbers constrain adjacent triangle count

#### C3. Shading for Elimination
- **Hitori** – Shade duplicate numbers so no number repeats in any row/column; black cells don't touch; white cells connected

#### C4. Maze Construction via Shading
- **Nurimeizu** – Shade entire rooms to create a maze from S to G; circles on shortest path, triangles not; no 2×2 of either color

### D. Number/Symbol Placement
Puzzles where the solver fills cells with numbers or symbols.

#### D1. Latin Square Variants
- **Sudoku** – Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box

#### D2. Region-Based Number Fill
- **Fillomino** – Fill grid with numbers forming polyomino blocks of matching size; same-sized blocks can't touch
- **Ripple Effect** – Fill rooms with 1 to N; repeated numbers in a row/column must be spaced apart by at least that number
- **Makaro** – Fill rooms with 1 to N; arrow cells point to the largest neighbor; same numbers can't be adjacent across rooms
- **Nansuke** – Fill blank cells with digits from a given number list, placing multi-digit numbers across/down

#### D3. Symbol Placement
- **Juosan** – Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers constrain the difference; runs limited to 2 vertically for — and 2 horizontally for |
- **Akari** – Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells indicate adjacent bulb count; all white cells illuminated, no bulb-to-bulb visibility

### E. Grid Division/Partitioning
Puzzles where the solver divides the grid into regions or blocks.

#### E1. Rectangular Partitioning
- **Shikaku** – Divide grid into rectangles each containing exactly one number equal to the rectangle's area

#### E2. Fixed-Size Partitioning
- **Five Cells** – Divide grid into pentominoes; numbers indicate surrounding block-boundary line count

#### E3. Shape-Constrained Partitioning
- **Sashigane** – Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends, arrows mark ends, numbers indicate block size
- **Double Choco** – Divide grid into blocks each containing matching white and gray sub-regions of identical shape

### F. Object Placement/Movement
Puzzles where the solver places or moves discrete objects within the grid.

#### F1. Placement with Visibility/Interaction Rules
- **Hebi** – Place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells; snakes can't touch or see each other from head direction
- **Evolomino** – Place growing polyomino blocks along arrows; each subsequent block adds one square to the previous shape

#### F2. Movement of Objects
- **Satogaeri** – Move circles within countries so each country has exactly one; numbers indicate distance moved; paths can't cross
- **Yosenabe** – Move all circles straight into gray areas; arrows don't cross; gray area numbers equal sum of entering circle values

### G. Hybrid: Shading + Connectivity Constraints (Block-Based)
- **Chained Block** – Determine black cells forming numbered blocks; blocks must chain at corners; no duplicate block shape/size within a chain

---

## II. By Constraint Mechanism

### Connectivity Constraints
*All white/shaded cells must form a single connected group:*
Nurikabe, Kurodoko, Hitori, Heyawake, LITS, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Usowan

### No 2×2 Constraints
*No 2×2 area can be entirely one color:*
Nurikabe, LITS, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Sto-stone

### Adjacency Prohibition (Black-Black)
*Shaded cells cannot share edges:*
Hitori, Kurodoko, Usowan, Yajilin, Norinori (partially—dominoes only)

### Visibility/Line-of-Sight Clues
*Numbers count cells or objects visible in cardinal directions:*
Akari, Kurodoko, Nurimisaki, Yajilin, Hebi

### Room/Region-Based Constraints
*Bold-lined regions impose local rules:*
Heyawake, Double Choco, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Five Cells, Sudoku, Norinori, Usowan, Tilepaint

---

## III. By Grid Element Used

| Element | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Numbered black cells** | Akari, Shakashaka, Hebi, Yajilin |
| **Circled numbers** | Kurodoko, Kurotto, Hashiwokakero, Satogaeri, Nurimisaki, Suraromu, Yosenabe |
| **Black/white circles** | Masyu, Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop |
| **Arrows** | Makaro, Sashigane, Evolomino, Hebi, Yajilin, Nagareru |
| **Bold-lined regions** | Heyawake, Double Choco, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Five Cells, Sudoku, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Norinori, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Usowan, Tilepaint, Chained Block |
| **Dots on grid intersections** | Slitherlink |
| **Moon/Sun symbols** | Moon-or-Sun |
| **Pre-placed numbers in cells** | Hitori, Fillomino, Sudoku, Nansuke, Ripple Effect |
| **Gates (dotted lines)** | Suraromu |
| **Gray/white cell coloring (given)** | Double Choco, Sto-stone, Yosenabe |
| **Diagonal clue cells** | Tilepaint |
| **Question marks** | Chained Block |
